habitat: Singly or in pairs in well-grassed woodland and thornveld of the drier regions. When approached it freezes, usually with its back to the observer.
summary: An uncommon visitor and resident. The white throat has a chestnut V. A dark brown band crosses the upper breast to the shoulders, and a chestnut band crosses the lower breast. The bill base, eye-ring and legs are yellow. The immature’s lower band is poorly defined. It is mainly nocturnal and calls chick-a-chuck-a-chuck-a-chuck, mostly at night. Newman calls it both a visitor and a resident, so status and months were left unset. The Kemp code VB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Bronze-winged Courser has red legs and a dark mask, without the two breast bands. Three-banded Courser has yellow legs and the chestnut and dark brown bands.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^4=16 mature individuals (visiting breeder); paper interval half–double → 8–32.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

head.pattern: Chestnut V-shaped collar on the white throat. Bold head markings.

underparts.pattern: Dark brown upper breast-band to the shoulders, and a chestnut lower breast-band. The bands span the breast and do not encircle the neck.
The lower band is poorly defined.

viewNotes.note: White throat with a chestnut V, then a dark brown band and a chestnut band.
Yellow eye-ring and a yellow base to the bill.
The back colour was not named. It often freezes with its back to the observer.
A separate flight pattern was not described. It is mainly nocturnal.
Dark brown upper breast-band and chestnut lower band.

calls.description: Mostly at night, chick-a-chuck-a-chuck-a-chuck. Grade A call from Awash National Park, Ethiopia. The filename uses the older name Heuglin’s Courser.
